references.text: God promises Abraham to give the land to his descendants, which is the first part of the promise referred to in Deuteronomy 1:8.
God makes a covenant with Abraham and promises to give the land from the River of Egypt to the Euphrates to his descendants.
God repeats the promise to give the land of Canaan to Abraham and his descendants as an eternal possession.
God confirms the promise to Isaac and promises to give him and his descendants all these lands, which He swore to Abraham.
God repeats the promise to Jacob to give the land to him and his descendants.
Joseph reminds the Israelites of God's oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to bring them into the promised land.
God says He will lead the Israelites out of Egypt and into a good and spacious land.
God promises to bring the Israelites to the land He swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God commands Moses to lead the people to the land He swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God says that the disobedient will not be allowed to see the land He swore to give to their fathers.
Moses reminds the people of the land God swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The land is given to fulfill the promise God swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God shows Moses the land He swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Stephen refers to God's promise to give the land to Abraham and his descendants.
Abraham obeyed in faith when he was called to go out to a land that he would receive as an inheritance.
